finding: The initial Treasury rally after the weak September payroll report failed to persist: by U.S. midday the 10-year yield was up 2.18 bp at 5.256% and the 2-year up 3.35 bp at 4.821%, even as October Fed-hike odds remained reduced near 21%. Gold also reversed an earlier >1% gain and fell about 1%, while equities remained higher.
net_new_delta: This directly advances the prior ICARUS falsifier. Weak payrolls materially reduced near-term Fed-hike expectations, but Treasury yields reversed their initial decline and moved higher the same session. That intraday failure of policy-path easing to deliver durable duration relief strengthens the existing hypothesis that long-end pricing contains material inflation/fiscal/term-premium forces not captured by near-term Fed-path expectations alone. It is evidence of decoupling, not proof of any single causal component.

evidence.claim: After initially falling on the 29,000 payroll print, Treasury yields reversed higher; 10Y was up 2.18 bp at 5.256% and 2Y up 3.35 bp at 4.821%. October hike odds were about 21%, Nasdaq was up more than 1%, and spot gold was down about 1.08%.

G7 countries agreed to a coordinated 100 million barrel diesel/crude emergency-stock release over four months, frontloading diesel within 20 days; diesel futures fell sharply, adding a contemporaneous energy-inflation relief impulse.

conflicts: Near-term Fed-hike odds fell after weak payrolls, yet both 2Y and 10Y Treasury yields reversed early declines and were higher on the day.
Gold initially gained more than 1% on the weak jobs report but reversed to a loss as yields stayed elevated, showing that the initial dovish cross-asset impulse did not persist.
Equities remained higher while yields reversed upward, so the session is not a uniform risk-off or growth-scare regime.
The G7 emergency-stock release is easing oil/diesel prices, creating an inflation-relief impulse that conflicts with still-elevated sovereign yields.
unknown: Whether the yield reversal persists beyond the payroll session.
The respective causal weights of inflation risk, fiscal/debt supply, term premium, growth resilience and positioning in the long-end reversal.
Whether the G7 stock release produces durable energy-price relief or only temporary inventory substitution.
next_decisive_check: Test whether 10Y/30Y yields remain elevated or re-approach recent highs while October Fed-hike probability stays suppressed and energy prices soften. Persistence of that configuration would strengthen policy-path versus structural-duration decoupling; renewed sustained long-end compression would weaken it.

oracle.finding: The prior decisive check fired: weak payrolls lowered Fed-hike odds, but Treasury yields reversed their initial rally and moved higher the same session. Upgrade confidence in policy-path versus structural-duration decoupling, without assigning the unexplained long-end component to a single cause.

supermesh_x.finding: Fresh Reuters cross-asset evidence separates payroll/Fed-path repricing, Treasury-duration behavior, gold, equities and the G7 energy-stock intervention. The conflicting channels are real and should remain separately provenance-tagged; no order-flow, positioning or liquidity mechanism is inferred.
